A1.justification: Both 22-page PDFs describe the same DATA framework and include the complete supplementary material. Text, equations, tables, and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original 3D detection experiments on DAIR-V2X-C, V2XSET, and V2XSIM, including baseline comparisons, ablations, robustness tests, and supplementary qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and their results in Section 4 and the supplementary material.

M1.justification: The CDAM, PTAM, and IFAM components, their objectives, and the training and inference procedures are unchanged in Section 3 and the supplementary implementation descriptions.

E1.justification: Both versions use DAIR-V2X-C, V2XSET, and V2XSIM for collaborative 3D car detection. Latency, pose-noise, turning, intersection, and other qualitative test scenarios are retained unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same 13 baseline rows, including HEAL, MRCNet, FFNet, and CoBEVFlow. Comparator participation also remains unchanged in the latency, pose-error, and supplementary qualitative comparisons.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, perception ranges, AP50/AP70 metrics, noise and latency settings, and model configurations are unchanged. Supplementary Section 2 retains the same three-stage training budgets of 40, 10, and 10 epochs.

E4.justification: Tables 2–4 retain the same component, temporal-stage/window-size, and distance-threshold ablations. Pose-error tests and supplementary turning, intersection, and synchronous detection case studies are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point-estimate reporting without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The reported Gaussian noise standard deviations remain experimental perturbation settings.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Tables 1–4 and plotted and qualitative results in Figures 7–13 are unchanged. For example, both report DATA's 65.48% AP70 on DAIR-V2X-C without latency and 75.58% AP50 at 500 ms latency.

T1.justification: Equations 1–26, the kinematic formulation, mathematical definitions, and supplementary Section 1.3's computational-complexity arguments are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning domain/time alignment, feature aggregation, state-of-the-art detection, and robustness to delays and pose errors.

C2.justification: Interpretations of density balancing, observability alignment, foreground enhancement, and temporal compensation are unchanged. The discussion of small-window degradation and prediction-stage error accumulation is retained, with no new limitations or qualifications.

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions, hyperparameters, optimizer schedules, batch size, and data-processing information remain identical. Both versions retain the same repository address and statement that code will be released.

R1.justification: The same 47 references and related-work discussions are retained. Reference reflow does not add or remove cited works or alter the paper's positioning.

P1.justification: v2 removes grant identifiers from the acknowledgments while retaining the funding organizations, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific prose, section organization, and supplementary text are unchanged.

P2.justification: The shortened acknowledgments reflow the references across columns and PDF pages 9–10, including splitting reference 24 across pages. Figures, tables, captions, and their placement remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 preserves the complete scientific argument, empirical evidence, mathematical content, and reproducibility information, including the supplementary material. Removing grant identifiers and slightly reflowing references produce no meaningful net change in the paper's overall quality.
